content:
Ravi Patel: CI started failing on the kernels image for the attention runtime. Link errors during the final shared object link step in the container. Failing job: build/flashkernels-prod. Error snippet below. Anyone seen this today?
CI-bot: Build #4627 failed: https://ci.internal.redwood/builds/4627 — link: undefined reference to '__cxa_throw_bad_array_new_length' (exit code 1) :warning:
Jordan Lee: that symbol smells like libstdc++/libgcc ABI mismatch. Is the container base image changed recently? debian vs ubuntu/glibc version can do this.
Maya Chen: we did flip some CFLAGS in the last merge (removed -fno-var-tracking-assignments). Also a packaging PR swapped the base image. Can you paste the exact linker command?
Ravi Patel: linker line:
```
/usr/bin/g++ -shared -Wl,-O1 -o libflash_paged.so build/obj/*.o -L/usr/local/lib -lstdc++ -lpthread -Wl,--no-undefined
```
and the tail of the error: 
```
/usr/bin/ld: build/obj/kv_cache.o: in function `allocate_aligned':
kv_cache.cpp:(.text+0x3f2): undefined reference to `__cxa_throw_bad_array_new_length'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
Theo Nguyen: on the perf side, we've seen subtle regressions when switching compiler minor versions. On a GCC13 build we measured ~6% higher L1d misses for the fused attention kernel vs GCC12. Perf record pointed to allocator code paths. Could be different inlined libstdc++ helpers.
Samira Ali: packaging note: PR #289 moved the runtime image from debian:bookworm-slim to ubuntu:22.04-slim to get newer docker tooling. That likely bumped glibc/libstdc++ ABI. We can either pin the base image or force-consistent toolchain in CI.
Jordan Lee: quick repro steps to validate locally:
```
docker run --rm -it ghcr.io/redwood/runtime-image:pr-289 /bin/bash
apt update && apt install -y build-essential cmake
g++ --version
ldd --version
ldd /usr/local/lib/libstdc++.so.6 || true
```
Check for mismatched SONAMEs and run `readelf -s` on libstdc++ used during link/build.
Maya Chen: also try building with -static-libstdc++ to confirm it's an ABI surface issue. If that fixes linking, we know it's runtime vs toolchain mismatch.
Ravi Patel: will try a CI job pinning GXX="/usr/bin/g++-12" and CFLAGS="-O2 -fno-plt" plus static libstdc++; kicking off debug build now.
Theo Nguyen: if you hit the build, please also run our perf smoke harness (scripts/perf/smoke.sh) inside the same container and upload the perf.data so we can compare hotpaths.
Samira Ali: created issue infra#744 to track: "runtime image toolchain drift causing linker/ABI failures" and linked the CI job.
Ravi Patel: thanks — I have a repro image and a failing build URL in the issue. tagging @Jordan for follow-up if my debug job is noisy :crossed_fingers: 
Jordan Lee: ack, I'll watch the build and try the readelf checks. If it's the image bump we should pin the base and add a CI assert that build-time and runtime libstdc++ SONAMEs match.
Maya Chen: tiny follow-up — we should also check CXXFLAGS ordering: LTO or -flto sometimes hides these until link. Try disabling LTO for the debug run.
CI-bot: New comment on build/4627 by Ravi Patel: "debug run pushed (image: ghcr.io/redwood/runtime-debug:1902504321)"
Ravi Patel: logging results to the issue, will update when perf and link are green.
